notes.2: Many candidates understood what is meant by the term species. Some candidates incorrectly believed that members of a species all look identical.
notes.6: While many candidates chose the correct option, some incorrectly believed that diffusion involves the movement of water only and that diffusion and osmosis require energy from respiration. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2023
notes.7: Few candidates understood that water acts as a solvent in digestion. Some candidates incorrectly believed that water is a mineral.
notes.10: Only a few candidates knew the processes that digestion and respiration depend on the action of enzymes. Osmosis does not require enzymes.
notes.12: Some care was needed in answering this question. Only in test-tube C was there an aquatic plant exposed to light. Having light, the aquatic plant can photosynthesise. This process will remove carbon dioxide from the surrounding water.
notes.13: Some candidates correctly identified the uses of carbohydrates in plants. Some incorrectly believed that glucose is used for energy storage, starch for cells and sucrose for respiration.
notes.16: Only a minority of candidates chose the correct option. Many candidates just read the figure for fibre from the label. The label showed the amount of fibre in 100 g of cereal, but the person only ate 45 g of cereal. Candidates needed to calculate (2.8 g ÷100 g) × 45 g.
notes.18: This question proved to be demanding for most candidates. It is important in such questions for candidates to study the information carefully. A low wind speed and a low atmospheric temperature will result in a low transpiration rate.
notes.19: A significant proportion of candidates were unable to identify the left ventricle of the heart.
notes.20: The features of arteries and veins were not well known by most candidates.
notes.21: Many candidates understood that the gas exchange surfaces in animals are thin-walled and have a large surface area. Some candidates incorrectly believed that the gas exchange surfaces in animals are thick-walled.
notes.23: This question was correctly answered by most candidates. Some candidates incorrectly believed that X represented the heart.
notes.24: For the molecule produced by anaerobic respiration in yeast, similar numbers of candidates chose carbon dioxide (correct) and lactic acid (incorrect).
notes.26: Few candidates were able to identify the relay neurone in a reflex arc. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2023
notes.28: Many candidates correctly chose the pancreas, option C . Some candidates incorrectly selected the adrenal gland.
notes.31: Many candidates understood that blood group, eye colour and sex are inherited in humans. Some candidates incorrectly believed that language is inherited but sex is not.
notes.32: Few candidates knew that the structure which contains enzymes that can digest the jelly coat of an egg cell is the acrosome. Some candidates incorrectly chose the flagellum.
notes.33: There was a lack of understanding by most candidates of what the term pure-breeding means.
notes.34: Most candidates were able to determine the correct answer, option D . It is important in genetic crosses like this that candidates work methodically through the information.
notes.35: Few candidates understood that continuous variation is variation that results in a range of phenotypes between two extremes.
notes.38: Only some candidates were able to identify the correct pyramid of biomass.
notes.40: Many candidates understood that bacteria are useful for manufacturing products for human use because they reproduce very rapidly. Some candidates incorrectly believed that bacteria can be grown without nutrients. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2023
